notes: Read all 88 source lines line by line before editing. The hook is a thin URL-state wrapper: it composes a `hidden_{chartKey}` param name and delegates to the sibling `useUrlArray` (web/src/hooks/useUrlState.ts -> react-router-dom useSearchParams) to persist a Set<string> of hidden chart dataKeys into the URL query string. The only browser-only behavior is that URL persistence; everything else (Set math, useMemo/useCallback, the public HiddenSeriesState API) is pure TS that ports 1:1.

L1 `import { useCallback, useMemo } from 'react'` -> `import { useCallback, useMemo, useState } from 'react'` plus `import type { Dispatch, SetStateAction } from 'react'`: useState backs the native in-memory shim that replaces URL state; the type-only import annotates the shim's setter return so the functional-updater contract stays explicit.

L2 `import { useUrlArray } from './useUrlState'` -> REMOVED and replaced by an inlined native `useUrlArray` shim (output L71-77). useUrlState is react-router-dom (useSearchParams) and is structurally unavailable on React Native (no address bar / query string). This mirrors the established native precedent that inlines a useState-backed useUrlArray per-file: SignalLogViewerPage.tsx L287-297 and PeriodComparePage.tsx L321-352. No './useUrlState' module is created (the codebase convention inlines the shim rather than introducing a shared native useUrlState).

L4-29 the file/hook JSDoc (purpose: URL-persisted hidden-series state; the useChartLegendState comparison; the ChartContainer/ChartLegend usage example L16-28) is preserved and adapted for native: the 'persisting to URL state so deep-links carry the toggle' framing (L7-8) and the 'URL state is shareable, cross-tab, survives reloads in private-mode' paragraph (L11-14) are restated as 'in-memory for the lifetime of the screen; the web URL-shareability / cross-tab / private-mode notes do not apply on native'. The tsx usage example (chartKey, ChartLegend state, Line dataKey/isHidden) is kept verbatim. Documented in the file header too.

L30-39 the `export interface HiddenSeriesState` (hidden: Set<string>; toggle: (seriesKey: string) => void; isHidden: (seriesKey: string) => boolean; reset: () => void) is preserved verbatim, including every per-field doc comment. The public API shape is byte-compatible so any native consumer is unaffected. Only the `reset` doc (L37) parenthetical 'drops `?hidden_{chartKey}` from the URL' is restated as 'resets the in-memory hidden set for this chart' since there is no URL.
L40-41 blank line + `const HIDDEN_PARAM_PREFIX = 'hidden_'` preserved verbatim (still used to build paramName; inert as a param name but kept so the chartKey threading is identical to web).

L42-56 the useHiddenSeries JSDoc (the sorted/comma-joined URL example L43-49 and the empty-chartKey / Rules-of-Hooks paragraph L51-55) is preserved: the empty-chartKey/no-op-param/Rules-of-Hooks guidance ports verbatim; the 'sorted, comma-joined list under ?hidden_{chartKey}=… bookmarkable view' framing is restated as 'sorted list kept in component state (no URL), preserving the toggle behavior without the shareability'.

L57-59 `export function useHiddenSeries(chartKey: string): HiddenSeriesState`, `const paramName = `${HIDDEN_PARAM_PREFIX}${chartKey}``, and `const [arr, setArr] = useUrlArray(paramName)` preserved verbatim — the call site is byte-identical; only useUrlArray's resolution changed from the './useUrlState' import to the inlined shim. setArr is typed Dispatch<SetStateAction<string[]>>, a superset-compatible replacement for the web UrlStateSetter<string[]> (useHiddenSeries never passes the web setter's optional second `options` arg, so the functional-updater + direct-value usages below typecheck identically).

L61 `const hidden = useMemo(() => new Set(arr), [arr])` preserved verbatim. Referential stability is maintained: native useState returns a stable `arr` reference until setArr fires (exactly as the web useUrlState memoized `arr` by raw URL string), so `hidden` stays stable across renders just like web.

L63-66 `isHidden = useCallback((seriesKey: string) => hidden.has(seriesKey), [hidden])` preserved verbatim, keeping the explicit `seriesKey: string` annotation (required under noImplicitAny; prettier keeps the parens for an annotated single param).

L68-81 `toggle = useCallback((seriesKey: string) => { setArr((prev) => { const next = new Set(prev); if (next.has(seriesKey)) next.delete(seriesKey); else next.add(seriesKey); return Array.from(next).sort(); }); }, [setArr])` ported verbatim; only `setArr((prev) =>` -> `setArr(prev =>` to satisfy the native prettier `arrowParens: 'avoid'` rule (`prev` is contextually typed string[] by SetStateAction so no annotation is needed). The Set toggle math and the `.sort()` canonicalization (web L74-77 comment) are preserved — the sort still yields deterministic, order-independent output; the comment is restated to note it kept URLs canonical on web and keeps the stored list canonical on native.

L83-85 `reset = useCallback(() => { setArr([]); }, [setArr])` preserved verbatim (clears the hidden set; on web this dropped the URL param, on native it empties the in-memory array — same observable effect: nothing hidden).
L87 `return { hidden, toggle, isHidden, reset }` preserved verbatim. L88-89 closing brace + trailing newline preserved.

Browser-only behavior (URL query-string persistence + cross-link shareability via react-router-dom useSearchParams) is documented as structurally unavailable in the file header, the inline shim comment, and these notes; the native fallback is explicit in-memory component state. No DOM-only modules, browser HTML elements, Recharts, Leaflet, or web UI components are imported — only react's useCallback / useMemo / useState. Gates run from apps/native: npm run typecheck; npm run lint -- --quiet; npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles.
